enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . 549 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 530 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

 - A cold front has pushed through today bringing continued 
   breezy and windy conditions with well below normal 
   temperatures.

 - High Wind Warning and Wind Advisory still in effect through 
   tonight for southwest New Mexico. Wind gusts to 50 mph are 
   possible in New Mexico bootheel.
 
 - Scattered rain showers for the middle of next week as 
   temperatures rebound. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Today, we will see our coldest temperatures of the season so far 
with lows dipping down to the low 40s through much of the 
lowlands. Area mountains will see subfreezing conditions with the 
Sacs reaching the low 20s in some parts during tomorrow's early 
morning. These temperature trends are about 15 to 20 degrees below
normal for this time of year. High temperatures will rebound by 
the end of the weekend. Widespread sustained easterly winds 
between 20 and 30 mph will continue this afternoon and evening 
with gusts exceeding 50 mph at times in parts of southern Hidalgo 
county.

Blowing dust remains a concern through this evening coinciding 
with the greatest wind threat in southern Hidalgo county according
to the signatures in the RRFS. A Blowing Dust Advisory near the 
Lordsburg Playa, NM Bootheel, and Luna county is in effect through
8 PM tonight.

Winds subside and precip chances are rather slim for most of the 
weekend with greater chances favoring the western half of the CWA 
on Sunday morning as a developing upper level low pushes east. 
This low deepens considerably over the course of next week 
bringing with it increasing chances for precip. Flooding is 
possible with areawide rain and PWs reaching around 1 inch. 
Confidence remains low for midweek rain impacts at this time.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 530 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

VMC through forecast period as gusty east flow diminishes 
overnight. Surface winds 080-110 at 10 to 15 knots with gusts up 
to 25 knots across SW NM and W TX through 06Z tonight. Lighter 
flow Saturday morning 070-100 at 5 to 10 knots, though gusts to 20
knots may linger at KDMN/KLRU overnight. Skies generally FEW- 
SCT170, with greater coverage east over W TX. East flow continues 
on Saturday, though lighter than today.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1200 PM MDT Fri Oct 16 2026

Winds remain breezy to windy today sustained between 25-30 mph, 
before subsiding late this evening. Lighter winds Saturday 
afternoon except locations bordering Arizona. Light winds of 5-10 
mph persist each afternoon through mid-week next week. Min RH's 
will begin to rise over the weekend starting in the upper teens in
the lowlands and reaching the 20s in higher terrain. On Sunday, 
these values increase as more moisture filters into the area. By 
next week, rain chances will continue to increase putting min RH's
over 40% by Wednesday. Ventilation rates range from good to very 
good today and drop to poor to good tomorrow. Rates Sunday will be
poor becoming poor to good early next week.
